ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing and continuous screening of every director, officer, shareholder, and UBO against FINTRAC administrative/risk indicators, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists (Special Economic Measures Act and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act domestic and Magnitsky lists), the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK and EU consolidated sanctions lists, and PEP/adverse-media databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for foreign PEPs, source of wealth and source of funds declarations are required for any wire transfers, and re-screening is required at least every 90 days or upon beneficial ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Quebec Enterprise Registrar portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet. A name in another script must be transliterated into Latin characters. Under the Charter of the French Language, the legal name and all mandatory corporate inscriptions must be usable in French in Quebec, and a French version of the name is required where the corporation carries on business in Quebec. The name must contain a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltée', or 'Société par actions'. Names that are only descriptive of goods or services, that are misleading, or that create confusion with existing enterprises will be refused.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Restricted financial terms such as 'bank', 'trust', 'loan', 'insurance', and 'financial institution' without prior regulatory approval from the Autorité des marchés financiers or other competent regulator
Terms suggesting royal, federal, provincial, or municipal government patronage such as 'Royal', 'Canada', 'Quebec', 'government', 'municipal', or 'federal' without ministerial authorization
Words protected by professional orders such as 'lawyer', 'notary', 'accountant', 'engineer', 'architect', or 'physician' unless duly licensed
Misleading terms implying a regulated securities, brokerage, or financial activity
Identical or confusingly similar names existing in the Registraire des entreprises or protected trademark databases
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire refuses a proposed name, the applicant may submit a corrected request online with a revised name or additional supporting trademark/user-name consents. A formal written reconsideration may be filed with the Registraire under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1. If the reconsideration is refused, judicial review may be sought before the Superior Court of Quebec pursuant to the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01. Name reservation extensions are not automatic; if the 90-day reservation lapses before incorporation, a new name reservation and search fee must be paid.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Quebec is mandatory and must be a physical street address capable of receiving service of process; post-office boxes are not acceptable. A virtual office is permissible for this industry only where a recognized corporate service provider maintains a physical office space in Quebec, upon which service of process may be effected, and where the provider does not act merely as a mail forwarding service. For ISIC 7020 ESG/carbon advisory and offset brokerage activities, virtual registered office acceptance is legally available, but financial institutions and wire-transfer counterparties will generally require additional actual commercial substance evidence before opening accounts or clearing large wire payments.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (below 10% annual probability) for a clean, low-risk ESG advisory and carbon accounting entity in the absence of triggering events; moderate (10-25%) likelihood materializes if the corporation engages in unlicensed money transmission, handles client funds, receives sanctioned counterparties, files inconsistent declarations, or becomes subject to FINTRAC/AMF investigation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, sections 9 (incorporation by articles) and 65 (registered office).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Incorporation may proceed with nil paid-up capital; escrow only required if shares are issued for property with special terms (not standard).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers' share subscription agreement be accepted and the initial estimated paid-up capital of the Corporation be fixed at CAD 10,000; RESOLVED that the directors approve the issuance of 100 common shares to the subscriber; RESOLVED that the registered office be established at [address], Province of Quebec, in accordance with the Articles; RESOLVED that [name] be appointed President, [name] as Secretary, and [name] as Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual meeting; RESOLVED that the Corporation adopt its by-laws, and the officers be authorized to execute all filings with the Registraire des entreprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises via Info-Centre or online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search through a certified service provider or the Registraire's online system. Submit a formal name reservation request for the corporate name 'X ESG Audit Inc.' (or French equivalent). The reservation is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Consent for use of name if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised name reservation within 15 days; alternatively, submit a statutory declaration supporting the requested name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in the prescribed form (PRO-1). Include corporate name, share structure, restrictions on transfer, and registered office street address. The incorporator signs the Articles; the document must be dated and filed with the Registraire.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a notice of defect, amend the Articles and refile within 30 days; the filing may be corrected without requiring a new name search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Directors and Initial Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises / Québec business records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Under the Articles, the incorporator appoints the initial directors in writing. After incorporation, the directors pass a first resolution appointing officers and establishing the registered office address. File a notice of registered office and board of directors with the Registraire.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to file officer changes may result in late-filing penalties; a rectification application can be filed within 60 days with payment of the applicable fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Shares and Initial Capitalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board authorizes the issuance of shares to the subscribers, records the share subscriptions in the securities register, and issues share certificates. No minimum paid-up capital is required; any amount contributed is deposited in the company's bank account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If there is a defect in the share issuance, the board must adopt a ratifying resolution and re-file the amended records within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Tax Accounts and Provincial Licenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File initial tax registrations through Revenu Québec (GST/QST) and obtain employer accounts for payroll, if applicable. This can be done via the online 'Clés en main' service. Also ensure compliance with the Quebec law on the preservation of business records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any failure to register for tax accounts can be cured by filing a late registration and paying a minimal penalty; interest charges are computed at the prescribed rate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenu Québec for provincial taxes and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal taxes
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities operating in Quebec must obtain a Business Number (BN) from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and a NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) from Revenu Québec. The SOP involves submitting incorporation documents, articles of incorporation, proof of legal status, and tax classification via the CRA's online portal or through a registered tax professional, followed by provincial registration with Revenu Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections available; however, hybrid mismatch election rules under the Income Tax Act and potential partnership taxation elections for specific structures

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 annual taxable supplies threshold for GST registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic reporting and digital tax stamps for GST/HST via CRA portal; Quebec requires electronic invoicing under the Act respecting the Québec sales tax with API integration for clearance

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating jointly with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential supervision; the Minister of Finance retains policy authority over exchange rate arrangements and the Foreign Exchange Reserves under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a full floating-exchange-rate regime with unrestricted currency convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. No exchange control legislation exists at the federal or provincial level; profit remittances, dividends, interest, and repatriation of capital are not subject to prior authorization or surrender requirements. Beneficial ownership and tax residency declarations under the Income Tax Act and common reporting standards are applicable, but no convertibility hurdle exists for legitimate commercial payments. The Canadian dollar (CAD) trades freely in global markets; banks process outward remittances with standard anti-money laundering (AML) and sanctions screening, not exchange control approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory timelines or mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts in Canada. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency in licensed bank accounts, repatriate proceeds on a commercially reasonable schedule, or use them for direct settlement of foreign obligations. FINTRAC reporting obligations apply only for transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 or equivalent under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and any suspicious transaction reporting is event-based rather than exchange-control-driven.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for offshore fintech EMIs: Low-to-Medium as primary banking relationship, High as auxiliary payment channel. Offshore digital EMIs are not regulated as banks in Canada and cannot provide a deposit-taking license equivalent to an OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank. They may operate as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) or Foreign Money Services Businesses (FMSBs) registered with FINTRAC, but such entities are prohibited from accepting Canadian client funds as 'deposits' without a valid OSFI authorization. For a professional ESG advisory entity, using an offshore EMI for initial treasury aggregation poses heightened AML scrutiny and operational risk; therefore the blueprint recommends maintaining a domestic Schedule I primary account and using an EMI only for low-value, non-client operational payments if the EMI is FINTRAC-registered.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is generally permitted by Canadian Schedule I banks for low-risk professional service corporations, subject to enhanced due diligence. Directors do not have to appear physically at a branch in all cases, but the bank's AML compliance officer may require a live video interview, notarized certificate of incumbency, corporate authorization resolution, and individual ID verification for each director, ultimate beneficial owner, and authorized signatory. A physical presence in Canada is not an absolute legal mandate; however, banks may impose a domestic registered address requirement for service of process and correspondence. For accounts opened from outside Canada or with non-resident directors, a higher-touch verification process including jurisdictional KYC checks and source-of-funds evidence is standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus: non-resident beneficial owner or director domiciled in a country outside Canada with opaque beneficial ownership registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry extract, certified articles of incorporation, register of directors and shareholders, notarized proof of identity with government-issued ID for each principal, proof of residential address, CV/resume for ultimate beneficial owner, and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for Canadian banking presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of inbound capital injection or large lump-sum equity funding from a related overseas entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany loan agreement or shareholders' equity subscription agreement, bank statement of originating account showing traceable funds, audited financial statements or certified accountant's confirmation of asset ownership, tax clearance or tax residency certificate of the funding entity, and a board resolution authorizing the specific wire transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Carbon accounting / ESG audit engagement creates a mismatched account-activity profile with high-frequency client disbursements or offset brokerage settlement flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed professional services engagement contracts, detailed fee schedule and carbon offset purchase agreements, invoicing ledger with supporting receipts, FINTRAC MSB registration if acting as an intermediary in offset payments, and a standard due-diligence questionnaire describing the compliance governance framework for client funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person (PEP) screen hits on a director, client, or counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal opinion from Canadian counsel on sanctions exposure, negative press news search log, sworn affidavit of non-involvement in sanctioned activities, resignation or replacement resolution if a PEP is minimized to non-signatory role, and confirmation of no connection to OFAC, OSFI, FINTRAC, or United Nations sanction lists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 with a clear corporate purpose code and reference. Under the Bank of Canada and payment clearing system rules, inward remittances are processed over the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the Real-Time Rail (RTR), depending on the paying bank's settlement membership. The applicant entity should provide the bank with a completed FX/Deposit Instruction, a board resolution allotting shares or recording the loan, and a statement of purpose using the Canadian banking convention: 'Business Investment – Equity Contribution' or 'Shareholder Loan – Working Capital'. The bank will verify the compliance of the originating institution against OFSI and United Nations sanctions lists, confirm the beneficial owner of the transmitting entity, and may require a copy of the commercial agreement or subscription contract. No approval from the Bank of Canada is required; the financing proceeds become immediately available after clearing unless a suspicious transaction report is triggered.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 for operational settlement, supplier payments, and subcontractor fees, with same-day or next-day clearing in CAD or USD. For carbon credit purchases from international registries or offset brokers, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) is permissible when the transaction is documentary and exceeds the bank's standard threshold; the LC terms must comply with the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP600). Alternatively, banks provide CAD/USD clearing via correspondent accounts at US Federal Reserve member banks for USD-denominated wires, and through the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) network for cross-border EUR, GBP, and other currencies. Underlying documents for each disbursement should include a pro-forma invoice, purchase order, service agreement, carbon credit certification, and a management-approved payment authorization form; there is no exchange control barrier, but the bank must perform sanctions screening on each beneficiary before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign exchange forward contracts (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) with maturities up to 12 months, widely offered by Schedule I banks for trade settlement and profit remittance hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CAD as an alternative only for counterparty pairs where a liquid deliverable market is unavailable, subject to OSFI market-risk capital and robust legal enforcement
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) between CAD and USD/EUR for larger treasury positions, executed under ISDA master agreements with bank-approved collateral arrangements
FX options (call/put structures) on CAD/USD for downside protection on carbon credit purchase liabilities and fee income repatriation, writing strategy limited to covered positions
Currency swaps and rolling spot forwards for managing conduit company and intercompany working-capital exposure, provided the bank's derivatives desk approves the corporate credit limit

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 50; failure to file for more than 12 months may lead to administrative strike-off and dissolution by Revenu Québec.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties under the CBCA; failure for three consecutive years triggers notice of dissolution from the Director.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) and Quebec CO-17 Corporate Tax Return

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the Canada Business Corporations Act, no audit is mandatory solely based on revenue; an audit may be dispensed with by unanimous shareholder resolution. Mandatory audit applies to public companies and corporations subject to specific regulatory regimes (e.g., financial institutions, federally regulated entities).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations in Quebec and federally incorporated private companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The corporation must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register and update it within 15 days of any share transfer or control change. The Quebec Annual Declaration to the REQ must confirm registered office, directors, and any changes in beneficial ownership; misrepresentation or omission may result in penalties and administrative dissolution.

stage_6.entry_description: Registered legal name, business number (BN), corporation type, fiscal year-end, and resident/non-resident status.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must indicate Canada branch status, list the PE jurisdiction, and attach Schedule 21? Actually for non-residents: 'insert the Canadian representative's name and address; do not claim SBD.'
